name: guards
summary: Hooks stop an agent's shell commands from running network code, using GitHub outside your owners, pushing past review, or polling in loops.
day: A prompt injection that tells an agent to pipe a script into a shell gets a refusal that names you, and the agent stops to ask.
cost: You run nothing. A hook checks each shell command before it starts.
risk: A guard can refuse a command you meant. The refusal says why and what to do instead. Every guard is off until you turn it on.

settings.question: Whom should a refusal tell the agent to ask, such as your first name?
settings.default: the person who runs this machine

settings.question: Which GitHub owners may agents use, separated by commas, such as you,your-org?
Which GitHub repositories take pushes straight to main or master, as owner/name separated by commas?
Which SSH public keys may sign the Git allowlist, one per line?

workflows.name: Shell guards
workflows.sentence: Agents cannot pipe network code into a shell, run a package the project lacks, change how Git maps URLs, use gh outside your GitHub owners, poll in a loop of turns, kill their own shell with pkill -f, skip Git hooks, force-push without a lease, or push to main of a repository that takes pull requests.

workflows.name: Signed Git allowlist
workflows.sentence: Git refuses any remote whose GitHub owner is not on a list you signed. With the shell guards on, gh follows the same list.
workflows.risk: Git refuses every remote outside the signed list, including other hosts than GitHub. Root, or anyone with sudo, can remove it. It stops mistakes, not a hostile agent. An agent that runs as you can override it with its own Git config, or edit the staged script before you run it with sudo.

workflows.name: Package age
workflows.sentence: Package installs through pnpm and Bun take only versions at least three days old, unless a project or you set another age.

workflows.name: OOM survival
workflows.sentence: Before memory runs out, earlyoom stops a runaway test or build, and T3's agent threads survive when the kernel kills a process inside them.

human.say: Install the signed Git allowlist as root. Fleet stages the list that verifies against guards.signers, and the root script checks the signature again before it writes /etc/fleet, the blocked-remote helper and the include in /etc/gitconfig.
human.command: fleet guards allowlist stage ~/.local/state/fleet/git-allowlist && sudo sh ~/.local/state/fleet/git-allowlist/install.sh
human.undo: Remove the Git allowlist as root: sudo sh ~/.local/state/fleet/git-allowlist/install.sh remove

human.say: Install earlyoom as root, so it stops a test or build at 10% free memory before T3 or the agents. It keeps an earlyoom config you wrote yourself.

checks.say: This machine runs a systemd older than 253, which ignores OOMPolicy=continue on T3's agent scopes. An out-of-memory kill still stops the whole agent thread here. Upgrade the OS to get systemd 253 or newer.
